newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African AIDS infection rate spiralling - expert.
newsitem.headline: S.African AIDS infection rate spiralling - expert.

text.p: South Africa has one of the world's fastest growing AIDS infection rates and five million of its citizens would be infected with the virus by the year 2000, an AIDS specialist said on Friday.

Clive Evian, who heads a Johannesburg-based AIDS unit, said socio-economic disparities created conditions conducive to the spread of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) which causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).
"Indications are that by the year 2000 five million people will be infected with the HIV virus," Evian told Reuters.
According to the latest statistics, about 1.5 million people are infected with AIDS in South Africa.
Evian said the infection rate of between six and 12 percent of the country's sexually active population -- aged between 20 and 40 -- was doubling every two to three years.
He said some of the world's previously highest infection rates in Malawi, Uganda and Zambia, had now slowed down.
He said the rapid infection rate would severely affect plans by President Nelson Mandela's government to redress apartheid imbalances.

"More people will start losing jobs and more will become destitute and affect development in the country. It is people in the parenting age who are getting the disease and they have dependents who are going to be destitute if the epidemic takes effect," Evian said.

He lashed out at the lack of cohesive AIDS education programmes and the 14-million rand ($3,036,876 million) musical show the Health Department commissioned earlier this year to liven the AIDS message.
